The classical period for averaging these variables is 30 years, as defined by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). The relevant quantities are most often surface variables such as temperature, precipitation and wind. Climate in a wider sense is the state, including a statistical description, of the climate system. Climate Change Mitigation Actions taken to reduce GHG emissions or increase the removal of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. Some examples include renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency improvements, and protection of forests that absorb carbon dioxide. Co-benefits Additional social, economic, or environmental advantages that arise from climate actions beyond their primary objective. For example, expanding public transport reduces greenhouse gas emissions while also improving air quality and reducing traffic congestion. Cost of Inaction The economic, social, and environmental losses that occur when climate adaptation or mitigation actions are delayed or not implemented. These costs may include damage to infrastructure, loss of livelihoods, health impacts, and long-term environmental degradation. Disaster Management A systematic process of planning and implementing measures to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters. It includes risk assessment, emergency preparedness, response operations, and post-disaster recovery efforts. xvi | Climate Change Adaptation in Indian Cities Exposure The presence of people, infrastructure, ecosystems, or economic assets in areas that may be affected by climate hazards such as floods, storms, droughts, or heatwaves. Outcomes The changes that occur as a result of project outputs. The outcomes typically relate to improvements in behaviour, capacity, or conditions, such as reduced climate risk, improved preparedness, or enhanced resilience of communities. Outputs The immediate and tangible results of a project or intervention. The outputs generally refer to activities completed or products delivered, such as infrastructure built, systems installed, or training programmes conducted. Sensitivity The degree to which a system, population, or sector is affected by climate variability or climate change. For example, agriculture that depends on rainfall is highly sensitive to changes in precipitation patterns. Vulnerability The degree to which a system, population, or infrastructure is susceptible to harm due to exposure to climate hazards and limited capacity to cope or adapt. Vulnerability is influenced by socio-economic conditions, infrastructure quality, and institutional capacity. 1. https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGI_AnnexVII.pdf LEARNING NOTE - 2 | xvii About Training Module Title Climate Change Adaptation Actions in Indian Cities Purpose This is the second of the six training modules being prepared by the Climate Centre for Cities (C-Cube) on climate and cities. In the first module, we showed that reducing Green House Gas (GHG) Emissions is the first priority to prevent an irreversible climate change of 2°C temperature rise that will disrupt existing life support systems. This second module focuses on understanding adaptation as a de-risking strategy of climate change. While mitigation action cuts current and future emissions, adaptation interventions can reduce the risk to lives and property from the climate change impacts of heat, flood and droughts. The module helps in developing a deeper understanding of climate action by all stakeholders.
